doc.title: Larry Ridley interviewed by Monk Rowe, Toronto, Canada, January 10, 2003

title: Playing with Lester Young's circle and Duke Ellington's humility
summary: He felt blessed to learn from Lester Young, Harry Edison, Vic Dickenson and Papa Jo Jones; Duke Ellington's warmth with everyone.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: Lester Young was beautiful. And to see Lester Young, Harry Edison and Vic Dickinson get together and Papa Jo Jones, those guys could talk man, and you wouldn’t know what the hell they were talking about. They had their own esoteric language. They could talk to each other and you wouldn’t know a word of what they’re talking about. And that’s why I feel so blessed that I had the opportunity to come up playing with all those guys. I mean and Joe Venuti and oh man, well if people go to the web site, I’ve got all the names, and I’ve been blessed.
You’ve been through the list, it’s great.

And I have just tried to absorb. And I always tell my students too, and even other people, you know like don’t get so cocky with such an attitude. The music is greater than all of us. Just because you think you know a little more than the average — I would say Duke Ellington, as great as he was, he could talk to just a person on the street, a homeless person, and make them feel like they were millionaires or heads of state, and he could go and talk to royalty and the same thing. And he always, he was fantastic. That was a hell of an experience for me to be around him. He was just — oh I don’t know what to say.
Well it’s partly a spiritual thing, don’t you think?
